systems.name: Access-Controlled Enterprise RAG
systems.headline: One question. Different correct answers.
systems.discoverySection: Frame the Round Around Different Correct Answers
systems.description: Keep unauthorised text out of model context using tenant partitioning, filtered retrieval and an authoritative post-check.
systems.question: Why did Vertex Financial lose data in March, and do they get service credits?
systems.scope: Read-only Q&A over the source scenario’s enterprise sources. Write actions and real-time streaming ingestion remain out of scope.
systems.provenance: Architecture, requirements and boundaries are adapted from the named canonical Markdown. Scenario branches, identifiers and payloads are illustrative teaching examples, not executions or measured results. Source assumptions remain assumptions.

discovery.question: Who are the users, and do they all see the same data?
discovery.answer: No. Tier-1, Tier-3, account managers, contractors and other tenants have different permitted answers.
discovery.decision: Start with a persona-by-document visibility matrix, not one universal answer.

discovery.question: What are the sources, and who owns permissions in each?
discovery.answer: The source scenario combines help content, runbooks, tickets, post-mortems, contracts/pricing and security advisories.
discovery.decision: Translate source ACLs into one resource model; refuse documents with unusable permissions.

discovery.question: What is the sensitivity range, and what regulatory constraints apply?
discovery.answer: The case includes public through restricted data, residency, PII, erasure and audit requirements.
discovery.decision: Use attribute-based deny rules and redaction obligations, enforced before model access.

discovery.question: What are the scale and latency budget?
discovery.answer: The lesson scopes the interview to multi-tenant Q&A under three seconds; it does not provide a universal traffic rate.
discovery.decision: Measure retrieval, reranking and generation; do not invent a throughput figure.

discovery.question: Can the assistant act, and what does a wrong answer cost?
discovery.answer: This design is read-only. Leaks are incidents; unsupported answers still need refusal.
discovery.decision: Exclude writes, separate quality from security, and gate releases on deterministic leak checks.

stages.what: A connector receives a changed source document. It must translate the source permission model along with the content.

stages.what: Validation finds no usable ACL. The record is refused and sent for connector correction, never into the tenant index.

revision.pitch: I would start by drawing the persona table: the same question must produce different correct answers. Access control therefore shapes retrieval. Ingestion translates source permissions, refuses unusable ACLs and indexes within a tenant partition. At query time, trusted identity attributes compile into a cheap search filter. Dense and lexical retrieval run under that filter and combine by rank fusion. Before any model sees text, an authoritative policy check re-evaluates live attributes and applies obligations such as redaction. Only that authorised pool is reranked and checked for enough evidence. The model drafts a cited answer, then citations are verified as real, permitted and supporting the claims. I would trace the actual context and separate forbidden-document labels from irrelevant-document labels in evaluation. Any leak blocks release. Non-security dependencies can degrade; authorisation cannot. If policy is unavailable, we refuse.
revision.flow: Authorise → plan → filtered hybrid retrieval → authoritative enforcement → rerank → grade evidence → generate → verify
requirements: Read-only multi-source Q&A, source permission translation, attribute-scoped hybrid retrieval, live enforcement, redaction obligations, evidence sufficiency, cited answers and replayable traces.
Tenant isolation, deny-overrides/default deny, live revocation, target below three seconds, graceful non-security degradation and a deterministic zero-leak release gate.
discovery: Who are the users, and do they all see the same data?
What are the sources, and who owns permissions in each?
What is the sensitivity range, and what regulatory constraints apply?
What are the scale and latency budget?
Can the assistant act, and what does a wrong answer cost?
revision.tradeoff: Tenant partitioning plus pre-filtering adds operational work but bounds the blast radius. The authoritative post-check adds a hop and catches live revocation and obligations the index filter cannot express.
revision.failure: A stale index returns a candidate after access was revoked. The live post-check drops it before model context and records the disagreement.
ops: Per-request rebuilding of a lexical index is the reference bottleneck. A production lexical store needs document-level security or correctly scoped shards.
Bound query expansion and measure model, reranker and search spans; the under-three-second figure is a target.
Cache embeddings by content hash, decouple ACL changes from content re-embedding, and bound model fan-out.
Use retrieval recall/MRR and groundedness for quality. Separately assert forbidden IDs never reach model context; any leak blocks release.
revision.remember: The filter makes retrieval cheap. The authoritative post-check makes it correct.
